requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`, so no implementation root is needed. Every clause describes behavior a client can observe.

- "The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an `instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty." This is an output rule. Any code that puts the field on the first delivery meets it, wherever the field is built or attached.
- "Text and structural searches share this rule." This is also observable: both search kinds must behave the same way. A version that duplicated the logic in each search path, instead of using one shared helper, would behave identically and still comply. The text names no shared interface, type or function.
- "Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field." This is state-dependent output. It could be tracked per conversation in any way, such as a flag, a counter or a session object, with the same results.
- "The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include in `used`." This sets the content of the string. The cited `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description` supplies context for that wording. It is a {cite}, so it adds no implementation duty here.

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field layout or delegation interface. Each clause could be satisfied by a differently structured implementation with the same runtime results. Tests supply the evidence for the behavior. With no review roots, nothing is missing.

behavioral: The test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` is marked `{test}` for the subject. It covers each obligation:

- **First delivery includes `instructions`, even with empty `matches`:** In `session`, the first successful search is `search_text` for `absent`. The test parses the result and asserts that `instructions` is a string (`as_str().unwrap()`) containing the expected phrases. It does not assert that `matches` is empty for this search. The pattern `absent` is not in the file, so an empty result is expected.
- **Per-conversation scope and the structural rule:** `fresh` is a separate session. Its first search, `search_text` for `hit`, returns non-empty matches, and `hits["instructions"]` equals `instructions`. `peer` is another separate session. Its first search, `search_structure` for `absent()`, asserts `matches == []` and `page["instructions"] == instructions`. So text and structural searches both carry the field, including with empty matches, and each new conversation gets it.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery:** In `session`, `search_text` with the invalid pattern `(` returns an error before anything else. The next successful search, `absent`, still carries `instructions`. This is tested for a failed text search. Failed structural searches are not tested, but the requirement does not distinguish them, so one failure class is enough.
- **Later searches and continuation pages omit the field:** The test asserts that `instructions` is absent in each of these cases:
  - the `get_next_page` result in `fresh`;
  - the later `search_text` in `peer`, after its first delivery was closed;
  - the later `search_text` for `hit` in `session`;
  - the second page from `get_next_page` in `session`.
- **Instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags go in `used`:** The test checks the phrases "Before submitting, close every delivered search page", "finish_search", "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read", "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result" and "without reading more source". The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description` is only cited, so it is context and needs no reassessment here.

I found no gap in obligations, assertions or markers.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
